how_to_apply: Log in to the Commission's website https://psc.ap.gov.in with the registered OTPR number. First-time applicants for any APPSC notification must first fill the One Time Profile Registration (OTPR) to obtain an OTPR ID, which is sent to the registered mobile number and email ID. OTPR alone is not an application.

Log in with the User Name (OTPR ID) and the password set. Click the "Online Application Submission" link at the bottom right corner of the website, then click "Fill Application" against the notification number to be applied for.

Check the OTPR data. Fill the application-specific data such as Local/Non-Local status and White card details, which are used to calculate the fee. To change any detail, use the modify OTPR link, save it and click online application submission again.
Fill the qualification details, post preferences and examination centre, then click "Save & Submit". Only then is the payment link generated; "Save" alone only partly saves the application.
Pay the fee through the payment gateway. The application is finally submitted on successful payment, and a payment reference ID is generated with an SMS to the registered mobile number.
If the payment fails, start a fresh payment process as in step 2. The filled application can be downloaded as a PDF for reference.
important_instructions: Applications by any mode other than the prescribed online mode will not be entertained. Incomplete or incorrect applications will be summarily rejected, and no relevant column should be left blank. The data displayed from OTPR at the time of submission counts for this notification; later OTPR changes are not considered. Reservation to BC-E group is subject to the adjudication of litigation before the Hon'ble Courts. Reservation: Women 33 1/3% and Meritorious Sports Persons 3% horizontally; no reservation for Persons with Benchmark Disability for this post. Recruitment is only for the notified vacancies and there will be no waiting list. Candidates must visit the Commission's website regularly; its information is final. Hall tickets will be hosted on the website. Objections to the initial answer key must be filed within three days of publication at Rs. 100 per objection, refunded for sustained objections. Furnishing incorrect information can lead to debarment for up to five years. Mobile phones, calculators, smart watches and other electronic devices are banned in the examination.

content_sections.heading: APPSC Eligibility Criteria 2026
content_sections.text: Applicants must hold the prescribed qualification from a recognised University as on the date of the notification (19-11-2026). That date is also the crucial date for calculating experience, including practical experience. Note I (printed below the qualification table): exceptionally good eye-sight, and colour blindness will be a disqualification. Note I also requires practical experience in a Forensic Science or Chemical or Analytical or Police Laboratory for at least 5 years. An applicant holding an equivalent qualification other than the prescribed one must produce a copy of the Government Orders to the Commission in advance, within 10 days of the last date for submitting applications. Otherwise the application will be rejected. The candidate must be a citizen of India. A non-citizen may be appointed only with the previous sanction of the State Government. The candidate must be of sound health, active habits and free from any bodily defect or infirmity rendering him or her unfit for the service, and of qualifying character and antecedents. Degrees through Open Universities or Distance Education must be recognised by the Distance Education Council, Government of India. B.Tech/B.E. courses under Distance Mode are eligible only if recognised or approved by AICTE. Candidates should check the official notification for the discipline-specific eligibility of each post.

rows.qualification_required: Must possess B.E. in Mechanical or Structural Engineering of its equivalent.
Must possess M.Sc. Degree in First Class or Second Class in Physics or its equivalent.
Must possess M.Sc. Degree in First Class or Second Class in Chemistry or its equivalent qualification OR B.Sc. Degree with A.I.C by examination in Forensic Science.

Must possess M.Sc. Degree in 1st or 2nd Class in either Botany/ Ecology/ Microbiology/ Biochemistry or its equivalent OR a Degree in Medicine with a Bachelor's Degree in Science (Chemistry, Botany, Zoology, Physics).

content_sections.heading: APPSC Selection Process 2026
content_sections.text: Selection is based on the Written Examination in online Computer based Recruitment Test (CBRT) mode, followed by a Computer Proficiency Test (CPT) that shortlisted candidates must qualify. Written Examination (objective type, degree standard), conducted by the Commission in CBRT mode. The date will be intimated later. After the written examination, candidates provisionally shortlisted in the ratio prescribed by the Commission have to qualify the CPT. Selection is post/post code wise, on merit in the written examination in the concerned subject, subject to qualifying the CPT. Minimum qualifying marks on aggregate: OC & EWS 40%, Backward Class 35%, SCs and STs 30%. Securing the minimum does not confer any right to selection. Appointment is subject to the selected candidate being found medically fit. Where candidates get equal marks, they are bracketed and ranked by age, the oldest first. If the age is also tied, the person who has the educational qualification at the earlier date is considered. SC and ST candidates not coming up for selection with the minimum marks are considered on rank, irrespective of the marks secured.

content_sections.heading: APPSC Exam Pattern 2026
content_sections.text: The Written (objective type) Examination is of degree standard, with Paper I common to all posts and Paper II in the subject of the post. The total for each post is 300 questions and 450 marks. Each wrong answer is penalised with 1/3rd of the marks prescribed for the question. Appearance in all papers is compulsory, and absence in any paper disqualifies the candidature. Paper I is set in English and translated into Telugu, with English as the authentic version. Subject papers are in English medium only. The test will be held at Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada, Tirupati and Ananthapuramu, and applicants choose three centre preferences; the Commission may allot any centre. If the CBRT is held in multiple sessions, scores will be normalised and results announced on percentile basis. If questions are deleted, scaling is done for that part of the paper. A General Mock Test is available on the Commission's website under the MOCK TEST option.

faq.question: Q1. How many vacancies are there in APPSC Assistant Director recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: There are 8 vacancies: 1 in Forensic Engineering, 2 in Physics, 2 in Chemistry and 3 in Biology.

faq.question: Q2. When can I apply for APPSC Notification 38/2026?
faq.answer: Online applications are accepted from 19 November 2026 to 13 December 2026 up to 11:59 P.M. through https://psc.ap.gov.in.

faq.question: Q3. What is the age limit for APPSC Assistant Director?
faq.answer: The age limit is minimum 18 years and maximum 44 years as on 1 July 2026. SC, ST, BCs and EWS get 5 years' relaxation, and other relaxations are listed in the age section.

faq.question: Q4. What is the qualification for Assistant Director in Chemistry?
faq.answer: M.Sc. Degree in First Class or Second Class in Chemistry or its equivalent qualification, or a B.Sc. Degree with A.I.C by examination in Forensic Science.

faq.question: Q5. Is work experience required?
faq.answer: Note I of the notice asks for practical experience in a Forensic Science, Chemical, Analytical or Police Laboratory for at least 5 years, and exceptionally good eye-sight.

faq.question: Q6. What is the application fee?
faq.answer: Applicants pay Rs. 250/- processing fee and Rs. 120/- examination fee. SC, ST, BC, Ex-Servicemen, White Card families of Andhra Pradesh and un-employed youth are exempted from the Rs. 120/- examination fee only.

faq.question: Q7. What is the salary of an APPSC Assistant Director?
faq.answer: The scale of pay is Rs. 57,100 – 1,47,760 for all four posts.

faq.question: Q8. How are candidates selected?
faq.answer: Selection is based on the written Computer Based Recruitment Test, with a Computer Proficiency Test to be qualified. Selection is post-wise on merit in the subject paper.

faq.question: Q9. Is there negative marking in the exam?
faq.answer: Yes. Each wrong answer is penalised with 1/3rd of the marks prescribed for the question. Each paper has 150 questions; Paper I carries 150 marks and Paper II 300 marks.

faq.question: Q10. Can I correct my application after submitting it?
faq.answer: Yes, for up to 7 days from the last date, at Rs. 100 per correction. Name, fee and age relaxation fields cannot be corrected.
